one_line: A browser-local document analysis workspace for sensitive financial and dietary files without uploading them.
what_it_does: Parses PDFs/OCR locally, exposes selected structured information to agents, and supports collaborative planning and charts.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent precise access to reviewed, locally extracted document state while preserving the central privacy promise; ordinary UI automation would be substantially less reliable for this workflow.
leverage_evidence: Pitch centers on agent access without uploading documents.
Description specifies local PDF text extraction/OCR, user review, mapping approval, and controlled agent access.
Single-tab human-agent collaboration replaces copy/paste and context switching.
execution_rationale: The described workflow is coherent and product-shaped, but the packet has no submitted video and visual execution evidence could not be verified; execution is therefore capped at plausible claimed scope.
execution_evidence: Demo is reported alive and gallery images are listed.
Description names an end-to-end flow from local extraction through review and plan generation.
impact_rationale: Confidential financial and health documents are a concrete audience need, and local processing directly addresses privacy concerns while retaining useful assistance.
impact_evidence: Explicit bank-statement and dietary-plan use cases.
No-upload/local-browser privacy proposition is directly aligned with sensitive documents.
creativity_rationale: The combination of browser-local document understanding, controlled agent access, and collaborative planning is a fresh WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: Privacy-first agent document workflow without server upload.
Human approval of extracted records and mappings is part of the interaction model.
usability_note: The one-tab workflow appears user-oriented, though visual usability was not verifiable from accessible evidence.
red_flags: No submitted video; execution claims rely mostly on narrative evidence.
standouts: Strong privacy/usefulness fit for local document processing.
WebMCP is tied to structured, consented access rather than merely exposing buttons.
advance_reason: Strong leverage and impact concept, with execution verification reserved for later evidence.

one_line: An agent-operated data-labeling studio where agents create annotations and humans review them.
what_it_does: Provides projects, image/video annotation, editing, augmentation, export, and WebMCP operations for boxes, polygons, and keypoints.
leverage_rationale: Structured annotation tools make high-volume, precise labeling feasible for an agent while keeping a human review loop; pixel-driven automation would be markedly less reliable.
leverage_evidence: Description reports roughly 30 WebMCP tools for projects, navigation, geometry editing, commit, and export.
Agent-labels/human-reviews is the product's central interaction model.
Claimed 1,500 direct labels in one continuous run demonstrates intended scale.
execution_rationale: The architecture and workflow are unusually complete for a labeling prototype, though no video was submitted and the packet cannot independently verify the claimed run.
execution_evidence: Public repository and alive demo are reported.
Detailed frontend/backend/storage/worker architecture.
Reported 0.99 Macro-F1 proof point.
impact_rationale: Computer-vision teams have a real, costly labeling bottleneck, and agent-assisted annotation with review could materially increase throughput.
impact_evidence: Explicit computer-vision labeling audience and hand-drawing pain point.
Reported continuous-run labels and model-quality result.
creativity_rationale: Moving from agent-generated markdown to a professional multimodal annotation studio, including gesture-based control-plane experimentation, is ambitious and distinctive.
creativity_evidence: Agent creates spatial annotations while reviewer supervises.
Sign-language/Codex Micro keyboard demonstration adds a memorable interaction experiment.
usability_note: A professional studio and review model are credible, but fine interaction quality is not verifiable without accessible frames.
red_flags: Several capabilities are explicitly said not to have been demoed.
standouts: Agent-native spatial labeling is a strong leverage case.
advance_reason: High leverage and meaningful audience value justify advancement despite incomplete execution evidence.

one_line: A shared container-yard workbench where humans and agents plan and execute safe relocations.
what_it_does: Models live yard state, blockers, rules, versioning, dry-run plans, authoritative moves, disruptions, audit provenance, and rewind.
leverage_rationale: The core product is shared semantic state plus optimistic concurrency between human and agent. Exact versions, dry runs, and recovery are difficult to reproduce comparably with pixel automation.
leverage_evidence: Agent tools expose blockers, constraints, legal destinations, versions, simulations, mutations, and recovery.
Destructive actions require the inspected expectedStateVersion and reject stale commands.
Human, agent, and system provenance are recorded on the same visual canvas.
execution_rationale: The described deterministic engine and state/recovery model indicate a coherent, intentionally scoped operational prototype; no video means end-to-end completion remains claimed rather than observed.
execution_evidence: Alive public demo and public repository reported.
Five-stack yard, deterministic logistics engine, audit trail, and rewind are specified as one workflow.
Narrative emphasizes conflict and stale-state recovery rather than only happy path.
impact_rationale: Container-yard operations have real coordination and safety costs; explicit stale-state rejection and recovery address a credible operational problem.
impact_evidence: Clear yard-operator audience and relocation workflow.
Safety rationale for preventing stale destructive actions.
creativity_rationale: The project turns optimistic concurrency and agent-human conflict recovery into the subject of a logistics product, an unusually deep WebMCP interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Shared live physical-plan metaphor with human/agent/system provenance.
Rewind and version-aware mutations are pursued as first-class UX.
usability_note: The semantic action model and visible provenance suggest strong operational usability; direct visual verification is unavailable.
red_flags: No submitted video, so claimed live behavior is not directly observed.
standouts: Exceptional WebMCP-native concurrency and recovery design.
Safety-aware distinction between simulation and mutation.
advance_reason: One of the strongest packets on WebMCP indispensability and human-agent shared state.

one_line: An incident-response desk where agents investigate traces and propose human-approved runtime guards.
what_it_does: Searches incidents, inspects traces, simulates guards, requests approval, applies approved guards, and produces audit reports.
leverage_rationale: Typed investigation, simulation, approval, and audit tools create a reliable safety-gated agent workflow beyond generic clicking, especially for policy-changing actions.
leverage_evidence: Six named WebMCP tools span investigation through approved deployment and reporting.
Final policy change is explicitly gated by human approval.
Provenance timeline records the approved action.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and appropriately scoped, but there are no frame sheets or video and the screenshot is packaging evidence only; completion cannot be verified.
execution_evidence: Public repository and alive demo reported.
Description presents a complete investigate-simulate-approve-apply-audit sequence.
impact_rationale: Incident responders face a real need for faster evidence analysis and safe remediation, and approval gating addresses the risk of autonomous policy changes.
impact_evidence: Specific security/AI incident-response audience.
Human-approved runtime guard deployment and audit trail directly address safety requirements.
creativity_rationale: The concept is a strong synthesis of incident response, trace analysis, runtime policy simulation, and agent approval controls.
creativity_evidence: Simulation-before-application and explicit approval are central interaction choices.
WebMCP is used for a complete response lifecycle, not a single command.
usability_note: The staged workflow should be understandable to responders, but visual evidence is unavailable.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets; execution confidence is low.
standouts: Good safety boundary: agent can investigate and simulate, human approves policy change.
advance_reason: Credible safety-focused agent workflow with strong impact, pending observed execution.

one_line: An AI learning platform combining course discovery, tutoring, purchasing, and payment recovery.
what_it_does: Answers educational questions, recommends courses, supports purchases and payment questions, and applies bounded revenue-recovery actions with escalation.
leverage_rationale: The assistant can act across course, payment, and recovery state, but much of the outcome could plausibly be achieved through conventional UI automation with some friction.
leverage_evidence: Description says the assistant interacts with actual courses, recommendations, payments, and recovery state.
Policy gate and human escalation constrain revenue-recovery actions.
execution_rationale: The product scope is broad and internally coherent, but there is no video and the packet provides only packaging screenshots; the central workflow is not evidenced end-to-end.
execution_evidence: Alive demo reported.
Detailed learning and payment/recovery flow is described.
impact_rationale: Students have a clear need for course navigation and contextual help, while payment recovery is a plausible supporting use case; breadth weakens focus somewhat.
impact_evidence: Explicit student audience and learning-navigation problem.
Assistant covers questions, recommendations, purchase support, and failed-payment assistance.
creativity_rationale: This is a competent education assistant with an integrated commerce/revenue-recovery angle, but the core category and interaction are familiar.
creativity_evidence: Combines tutoring/course discovery with bounded payment-recovery workflow.
Human escalation is included in the recovery pipeline.
usability_note: An integrated assistant could reduce navigation burden, but login and broad scope may add complexity; UI quality is unverified.
red_flags: Broad claims across education, purchasing, and payment operations are not end-to-end evidenced.
standouts: Policy-gated revenue recovery is a more specific workflow than a generic tutor.
advance_reason: Plausible product and audience, but leverage and execution evidence are too limited relative to the stronger packets.

one_line: A shared visual canvas where people and agents edit, discuss, and record decisions together.
what_it_does: Combines an Excalidraw board, anchored discussions, decisions, realtime multiplayer, semantic agent tools, revision checks, and idempotent writes.
leverage_rationale: The product exposes live board semantics, selection, viewport, discussion, revision, and safe writes directly to agents; generic automation cannot reliably reconstruct this shared state.
leverage_evidence: Typed tools read/edit canvas elements, add diagrams near focus, ask/reply, and record decisions.
Writes require the read revision and idempotency key, rejecting stale mutations.
Human and agent share durable board state while private focus remains private.
execution_rationale: The described architecture and collaboration model are cohesive and unusually complete, though submitted visual execution cannot be verified from the packet.
execution_evidence: Public repository and alive demo reported.
Detailed IndexedDB, Durable Object, WebSocket, auth, revision, and idempotency design.
Product workflow covers canvas, discussion, decisions, and multiplayer.
impact_rationale: Design and planning teams have a real need to combine visual artifacts with discussion and decisions; agent participation can reduce context loss.
impact_evidence: Clear collaborative visual-workspace audience.
Anchored discussion and durable decision records address real coordination gaps.
creativity_rationale: The shared visual board plus private agent focus, semantic spatial editing, and concurrency-safe collaboration is a genuinely original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Agents operate on semantic board state and user focus rather than screenshots.
Private focus/selection coexists with shared durable collaboration.
Stale-write rejection and idempotency are integrated into creative collaboration.
usability_note: The model is well matched to visual collaboration, though actual interaction polish is not directly verifiable.
red_flags: No submitted video; visual execution remains claimed.
standouts: Excellent semantic bridge between spatial human work and agent actions.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and creativity with a credible collaboration use case.

one_line: A browser-local shift-roster planner where an agent proposes and an exact solver proves feasibility.
what_it_does: Solves constrained rosters in WebAssembly, reports optimal/infeasible/timeout, supports human confirmation, audit receipts, and availability queries.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects agent conversation to precise solver-backed state and human confirmation; ordinary automation cannot provide reliable constraint proofs, stale-state handling, and structured receipts.
leverage_evidence: Transcript states six tools, three read and three write, with a real browser-constrained workflow.
Exact mixed-integer solver returns optimal, infeasible, or timeout rather than guesses.
Tool call remains open for a real human confirmation click; receipts are rederivable.
execution_rationale: The 176-second video transcript provides unusually strong end-to-end evidence: solve, conflict explanation, confirmation, published roster, and availability query, reinforced by tests and eval steps.
execution_evidence: Video is 176 seconds with an unbroken session and explicit tool invocation narrative.
Transcript demonstrates 42 shifts, a Friday-off conflict, exact named rules, approval/decline behavior, and published result.
Claims 190 tests, 34 real-browser assertions, and 55 no-model/no-key eval steps.
impact_rationale: Managers have a concrete high-stakes scheduling problem where plausible-but-invalid rosters cause operational and legal harm; exact infeasibility explanations provide credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific 10-person/33-rule roster audience and coverage/rest/contract constraints.
Solver proof distinguishes infeasible schedules and identifies conflicting rules.
Browser-local privacy suits sensitive names, pay rates, and absences.
creativity_rationale: The agent-proposes/solver-proves/human-decides interaction is memorable, technically ambitious, and pursued deeply through confirmation semantics and proof receipts.
creativity_evidence: Custom confirmation API built around WebMCP's lack of confirmation support.
Availability query checks every candidate by re-solving the entire week.
No-fourth-branch design prevents plausible fabricated schedules.
usability_note: The staged proposal, proof, and human decision model is clear and operationally appropriate.
standouts: Strongest packet-level execution evidence in this review.
Solver-backed guarantees are central, not decorative.
Privacy and human judgment are integrated into the core workflow.
advance_reason: Exceptional across all four scored criteria, with direct end-to-end video evidence.

one_line: A shared family care dashboard where agents help with care administration while humans confirm high-stakes actions.
what_it_does: Supports care tasks, appointments, benefits drafts, medication-change proposals, official-form submission, and human confirmation via WebMCP interaction.
leverage_rationale: Structured shared care state plus explicit human confirmation for irreversible/safety-relevant operations creates a safer agent workflow than generic UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Seven real tools span tasks, appointments, benefits, medication proposals, and official forms.
Irreversible or safety-relevant tools pause through requestUserInteraction for exact human review.
Shared family care circle is the stated human-agent workspace.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and safety-aware, but no video or frame sheets were submitted and demo status is unknown, so execution evidence is thin.
execution_evidence: Public repository reported.
Detailed care-management scope and confirmation boundary are described.
impact_rationale: Family caregivers face a real, burdensome, and sometimes high-stakes administrative load; assistance with a human gate has strong credible value.
impact_evidence: Specific caregiver tasks: medications, appointments, insurance, benefits, provider calls.
Safety distinction between reversible administration and dosage/forms actions.
creativity_rationale: The concept applies WebMCP's human-in-the-loop boundary to family caregiving, where the difference between drafting and committing is materially meaningful.
creativity_evidence: Care circle is shared by family members and agents.
Exact confirmation of safety-relevant actions is built into the tool model.
usability_note: The human-confirmation boundary should support trust, though the live UI and accessibility cannot be checked.
red_flags: No video or frame sheets; safety-critical execution is unverified.
standouts: High-impact care use case with an appropriately conservative authority boundary.
advance_reason: High impact and thoughtful safety design merit advancement, contingent on later execution verification.

one_line: A radiology capacity cockpit that balances scanners, patients, and qualified clinical staff across hospitals.
what_it_does: Combines scanner telemetry, patient queues, workforce expertise, simulations, suggested moves, audit logging, and human-gated agent orchestration.
leverage_rationale: Agents operate on live operational capacity and simulation state with human gating; structured orchestration is more reliable than clicking across a complex clinical dashboard.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly connects live scanner, queue, workforce, and WebMCP agent state.
Simulate/suggest/audit workflow is designed around human approval.
Operational cockpit exposes several linked constraints that are difficult to infer from pixels.
execution_rationale: The dashboard concept is coherent and richly specified, but no video/frame sheets were submitted and evidence is limited to packaging and narrative.
execution_evidence: Public repository and alive demo reported.
Multiple dashboard surfaces are named: coverage/load, simulation, suggested move, audit, patient status.
impact_rationale: Radiology delays and uneven scanner/workforce utilization are credible clinical operations problems, and better balancing could improve access and throughput.
impact_evidence: Specific hospital/radiology audience and capacity problem.
Proposed responses cover overload, fatigue, understaffing, and qualified routing.
creativity_rationale: The cross-hospital balancing cockpit is ambitious and useful, though orchestration dashboards are a familiar category and the novel interaction is less deeply evidenced.
creativity_evidence: Connects scanner capacity, patient queues, and human expertise as a living system.
Human-gated agent suggestions are integrated into the operational model.
usability_note: A unified cockpit could reduce coordination friction, but clinical usability and safety details are unverified.
red_flags: No submitted video or frame sheets.
High-stakes clinical claims are narrative-only in this packet.
standouts: Clear high-impact operational target with a credible human-gated posture.
advance_reason: Strong audience and impact case, but later evidence must validate the clinical workflow and execution.

one_line: A portfolio context manager where agents find evidence, create visitor takeaways, and prepare editable project briefs.
what_it_does: Adds structured profile, relevance ranking, visitor briefing, confirmed takeaway/PDF creation, and editable inquiry preparation to a portfolio.
leverage_rationale: The canonical evidence layer lets agents work with reviewed portfolio facts and visitor context rather than scrape presentation pages and guess; the resulting brief remains human-reviewed.
leverage_evidence: Five WebMCP tools establish profile, rank evidence, create visible briefing, save confirmed takeaway, and prepare project brief.
Takeaway creation requires explicit visitor confirmation for an unguessable public link.
Inquiry is prepared and prefilled but never sent, preserving human control.
execution_rationale: The workflow is coherent and thoughtfully bounded, with public repo/alive demo and frame sheets listed, but no transcript and no directly verified frame observations limit certainty.
execution_evidence: Public repository and alive demo reported.
Description covers evidence ranking through editable brief and confirmation boundaries.
Human-visible/reversible page changes are part of the stated design.
impact_rationale: Recruiters, founders, CTOs, and design leaders have a real need to quickly assess relevant portfolio proof and prepare a focused conversation; value is credible but audience is narrower.
impact_evidence: Explicit professional-visitor audience and browsing/context-repetition problem.
Output is a tailored evidence-backed takeaway and project brief.
creativity_rationale: Turning a portfolio into a visitor-specific, evidence-grounded context manager is a fresh synthesis beyond static browsing, with useful human-review boundaries.
creativity_evidence: Canonical profile plus visitor-context ranking and durable takeaway.
Agent prepares but does not send the inquiry, maintaining a deliberate collaboration boundary.
usability_note: The staged, editable briefing flow appears well matched to professional visitors; detailed UI verification is unavailable.
red_flags: No transcript; visual evidence could not be independently inspected.
Narrowly tailored to one portfolio context, which limits generality but is not an eligibility issue.
standouts: Strong evidence-grounding and explicit consent boundaries for generated takeaways.
Human-reviewed brief bridges browsing and conversation preparation.
advance_reason: Good WebMCP leverage and a specific, credible workflow with thoughtful trust boundaries.
